title: MATH2010 Module 01: Systems of Linear Equations

questions.q: Which of the following are linear equations in the variables x1, x2, x3?
questions.explain: A linear equation can be written as c1x1 + ... + cnxn = b with constant coefficients. π and √3 are just constants. 3(x1 - x2) = x3 + 4 rearranges to 3x1 - 3x2 - x3 = 4. The others have a product of variables (x1·x3), a variable in a denominator (2/x2), or a squared variable (x1²).

questions.q: A linear system is called consistent if:
choices: it has at least one solution
every equation in it is linear
questions.explain: Consistent means the solution set is not empty, so there is at least one solution. A consistent system can have exactly one solution or infinitely many.

questions.q: What is the one-word name for a linear system that has no solution (its solution set is empty)?
questions.explain: A system with no solution is inconsistent. A system with at least one solution is consistent.

questions.q: True or false: some linear system has exactly two solutions.
questions.explain: Every linear system has exactly one of these: no solution, exactly one solution, or infinitely many solutions. Exactly two is impossible.

questions.q: True or false: if a linear system has two different solutions, then it has infinitely many solutions.
questions.explain: The only possibilities are none, exactly one, or infinitely many. A system with two different solutions has more than one solution, so it must have infinitely many.

questions.q: Which of these triples (x1, x2, x3) are solutions of the system x1 + x2 + x3 = 3, x1 - x2 = 0?
questions.explain: A solution of a system must satisfy every equation. All five triples satisfy x1 + x2 + x3 = 3, but (1, 2, 0) and (3, 0, 0) fail x1 - x2 = 0. The first three satisfy both equations. Because the system has more than one solution, it has infinitely many.

questions.q: Each equation in a system of two linear equations in x and y has a line as its graph. If the two lines are parallel and different, how many solutions does the system have?
questions.explain: A solution is a point that lies on both lines. Parallel lines that are different never meet, so no point lies on both. Lines that cross give exactly one solution, and two copies of the same line give infinitely many.

questions.q: Which of the following are elementary row operations?
choices: Multiply every entry of R3 by -1/2
Multiply every entry of R2 by 0
Replace R1 by the entry-by-entry product of R1 and R2
Add 3 to every entry of R2
questions.explain: There are three elementary row operations: replacement (add a multiple of another row), interchange, and scaling by a NON-ZERO scalar. Scaling by 0 is not allowed. Multiplying rows together and adding a constant to every entry are not row operations, and they change the solution set.

questions.q: True or false: two linear systems are called equivalent if they have the same solution set.
questions.explain: This is the definition of equivalent systems. Replacement, interchange, and scaling by a nonzero scalar all produce an equivalent system.

questions.q: True or false: the replacement R2 ← R2 - 5R1 changes both row 1 and row 2.
questions.explain: Only the target row (row 2) changes. Row 1 is used to compute the new row 2, but row 1 itself stays the same.

questions.q: Apply R2 ← R2 - 3R1 to the augmented matrix [1 2 | 4; 3 5 | 7] (rows separated by semicolons). What is the new row 2?
questions.explain: New R2 = [3 - 3(1), 5 - 3(2) | 7 - 3(4)] = [0, -1 | -5]. Apply the operation to the whole row, including the right-hand side. [0 -1 | 7] forgets the augmented column, and [6 11 | 19] adds 3R1 instead of subtracting it.

questions.q: Why is multiplying a row (equation) by 0 NOT allowed as an elementary row operation?
choices: It can change the solution set, because it wipes out that equation and cannot be undone
It always makes the system inconsistent
It is allowed; only multiplying by 1 is forbidden
questions.explain: Scaling by 0 turns an equation into 0 = 0, which throws away a condition. The new system can have extra solutions, so it is not equivalent to the original. Scaling by a nonzero c can be undone by scaling by 1/c.

questions.q: True or false: if the augmented matrices of two linear systems are row equivalent, then the two systems have the same solution set.
questions.explain: Elementary row operations never change the solution set. Row equivalent means one matrix is reached from the other by a finite sequence of such operations, so the systems are equivalent. This is why solving the row-reduced matrix solves the original system.

questions.q: The augmented matrix [7 5 3 | 12; -6 1 -3 | -23; 2 0 1 | 7] has a leading 7 in row 1. Which single elementary row operation produces a 1 in the top-left position without introducing fractions?
questions.explain: R1 + R2 = [7 - 6, 5 + 1, 3 - 3 | 12 - 23] = [1 6 0 | -11]. Scaling by 1/7 gives a 1, but it puts fractions in the rest of the row (5/7, 3/7, 12/7). R1 - R2 gives a leading 13, and R1 ↔ R3 gives a leading 2.

questions.q: During row reduction, row 2 is [0 0 9 13 | -31] and row 3 is [0 0 2 3 | -7]. Which single elementary row operation makes the third entry of row 2 equal to 1 without introducing fractions?
questions.explain: R2 - 4R3 = [0, 0, 9 - 8, 13 - 12 | -31 + 28] = [0 0 1 1 | -3]. A replacement may use a row below the target row. (1/9)R2 gives a 1 but also 13/9 and -31/9. R2 - 9R3 gives -9, and the interchange puts a 2 there.

questions.q: A linear system has 4 equations in 6 variables. How many columns does its augmented matrix have?
questions.explain: A system of m equations in n variables has an m x (n+1) augmented matrix: one column per variable plus one column of right-hand sides. Here that is 4 x 7.

questions.q: What is the size of the coefficient matrix of a system of 3 equations in 5 variables?
questions.explain: The coefficient matrix is m x n: one row per equation (3) and one column per variable (5). The augmented matrix would be 3 x 6.

questions.q: Which is the augmented matrix of the system x1 - 2x3 = 5, 3x2 + x3 = -1, x1 + x2 = 0? (Rows are separated by semicolons.)
questions.explain: Keep the variables in the order x1, x2, x3 in every row, and write 0 for any missing variable. Row 1 is x1 + 0x2 - 2x3 = 5. Row 2 is 0x1 + 3x2 + x3 = -1. Row 3 is x1 + x2 + 0x3 = 0.

questions.q: In the general linear system with equations a_i1·x1 + a_i2·x2 + ... + a_in·xn = b_i, what is the entry a_23?
choices: The coefficient of x3 in equation 2
The coefficient of x2 in equation 3
The product of the 2nd and 3rd coefficients
questions.explain: In a_ij, the first index i is the equation (row) and the second index j is the variable (column). So a_23 is in row 2, column 3, which is the coefficient of x3 in equation 2.

questions.q: The augmented matrix [2 -1 0 | 4; 0 1 5 | -3] represents which system in x1, x2, x3?
questions.explain: Each row is one equation. The first three columns are the coefficients of x1, x2, x3, and the last column is the right-hand side. Row 1 is 2x1 - x2 + 0x3 = 4, and row 2 is 0x1 + x2 + 5x3 = -3.

questions.q: Classify the matrix [1 3 0 2; 0 0 1 -4; 0 0 0 0] (rows separated by semicolons).
questions.explain: The leading entries are 1s in columns 1 and 3, and they step to the right. The zero row is at the bottom. Each leading 1 is the only nonzero entry in its column. Columns 2 and 4 are not pivot columns, so their entries (3, 2, -4) can be anything.

questions.q: Classify the matrix [2 1 3; 0 0 5; 0 0 0].
questions.explain: It satisfies the three echelon conditions: the zero row is at the bottom, the leading entries (2 in column 1, 5 in column 3) step right, and there are zeros below them. It is not reduced because the leading entries are not 1, and column 3 has a nonzero entry (3) above its leading entry.

questions.q: Classify the matrix [1 0 0; 0 0 0; 0 1 0].
questions.explain: A zero row (row 2) sits above a nonzero row (row 3). This breaks the first echelon condition: all nonzero rows must be above any rows of all zeros.

questions.q: Classify the matrix [0 1 4; 1 0 2].
questions.explain: The leading entry of row 2 is in column 1, which is to the LEFT of the leading entry of row 1 (column 2). Each leading entry must be to the right of the one in the row above. Interchanging the rows would give reduced echelon form.

questions.q: Classify the matrix [1 2 0 3; 0 1 0 1; 0 0 1 2].
questions.explain: The leading 1s in columns 1, 2, 3 form a staircase with zeros below, so the matrix is in echelon form. It is not reduced because column 2 contains a leading 1 (row 2) with a nonzero entry (2) above it. R1 ← R1 - 2R2 would fix that.

questions.q: Classify the matrix [0 1 -3 0; 0 0 0 1].
questions.explain: The leading entries are 1s in column 2 (row 1) and column 4 (row 2), stepping to the right. Each leading 1 is the only nonzero entry in its column. A matrix in reduced echelon form can start with a zero column, and the non-pivot column 3 can contain anything.

questions.q: True or false: every matrix has exactly one echelon form.
questions.explain: Different sequences of row operations can give different echelon forms of the same matrix, for example by scaling a row. The REDUCED echelon form is unique. The leading entries of every echelon form are always in the same positions.

questions.q: True or false: every matrix is row equivalent to one and only one matrix in reduced echelon form.
questions.explain: The reduced echelon form of a matrix is unique. This is why different correct sequences of row operations always end at the same RREF and the same solution set.

questions.q: Which conditions are part of the definition of echelon form (not necessarily reduced)?
choices: All nonzero rows are above any rows of all zeros
Each leading entry is in a column to the right of the leading entry of the row above it
All entries in a column below a leading entry are zeros
Each leading entry is the only nonzero entry in its column
questions.explain: Echelon form has three conditions: zero rows at the bottom, leading entries stepping right, and zeros below each leading entry. 'Leading entry is 1' and 'only nonzero entry in its column' are the two extra conditions for REDUCED echelon form. Any rectangular matrix can be in echelon form.

questions.q: The Row Reduction Algorithm has a forward phase and a backward phase. What does each phase produce?
choices: Forward: an echelon form. Backward: the reduced echelon form.
Forward: the reduced echelon form. Backward: an echelon form.
Forward: the coefficient matrix. Backward: the augmented matrix.
Forward: the solution. Backward: a check of the solution.
questions.explain: The forward phase works down the matrix, making zeros below each pivot, and ends with an echelon form. The backward phase works up from the lowest pivot, scaling pivots to 1 and making zeros above them, and ends with the reduced echelon form.

questions.q: True or false: a row of all zeros has a leading entry equal to 0.
questions.explain: The leading entry of a row is its leftmost NONZERO entry. A zero row has no nonzero entries, so it has no leading entry at all.

questions.q: Which columns of A = [1 -2 3; 2 -4 7; -1 2 -1] are pivot columns?
questions.explain: R2 ← R2 - 2R1 gives [0 0 1]. R3 ← R3 + R1 gives [0 0 2]. R3 ← R3 - 2R2 gives [0 0 0]. The echelon form [1 -2 3; 0 0 1; 0 0 0] has leading entries in column 1 (row 1) and column 3 (row 2).

questions.q: What is a pivot position in a matrix A?
choices: A location in A that corresponds to a leading entry in an echelon form of A
Any entry of A that equals 1
The position of the largest entry in each column of A
Any nonzero entry in the first row of A
questions.explain: A pivot position is a location (row, column), found by row reducing A to an echelon form and noting where the leading entries are. A pivot column is a column of A that contains a pivot position.

questions.q: True or false: the entry of the ORIGINAL matrix A that sits in a pivot position must be nonzero.
questions.explain: Pivot positions are locations, not values. For A = [0 1; 1 0], interchanging the rows gives the echelon form [1 0; 0 1], so (row 1, column 1) is a pivot position, yet A has a 0 there.

questions.q: The reduced echelon form of the augmented matrix of a system in x1, x2, x3, x4 is [1 0 3 0 | 2; 0 1 -1 0 | 5; 0 0 0 1 | -4]. Which variables are free?
questions.explain: The pivot columns of the coefficient part are columns 1, 2, and 4, so x1, x2, x4 are basic. Column 3 has no pivot, so x3 is free. The last column is not a pivot column, so the system is consistent.

questions.q: The reduced echelon form of the augmented matrix of a system in x1, x2, x3, x4 is [1 0 3 0 | 2; 0 1 -1 0 | 5; 0 0 0 1 | -4]. What is the general solution?
choices: x1 = 2 - 3x3, x2 = 5 + x3, x3 free, x4 free
questions.explain: Row 1 says x1 + 3x3 = 2, so x1 = 2 - 3x3. Row 2 says x2 - x3 = 5, so x2 = 5 + x3. Row 3 says x4 = -4. Column 3 has no pivot, so x3 is free. Moving a free-variable term to the right side flips its sign.

questions.q: A consistent linear system has 3 equations in 5 variables, and its coefficient matrix has 3 pivot columns. How many free variables does it have?
questions.explain: Each pivot column gives a basic variable, and each non-pivot column of the coefficient matrix gives a free variable. 5 variable columns - 3 pivot columns = 2 free variables, so there are infinitely many solutions.

questions.q: Pivot columns of the coefficient matrix correspond to basic variables. What are the variables that correspond to NON-pivot columns called?
questions.explain: Non-pivot columns correspond to free variables, also called parameters. A free variable can take any value, and the basic variables are then determined by the free ones.

questions.q: True or false: the rightmost column of an augmented matrix can correspond to a free variable.
questions.explain: The rightmost column holds the constants, not a variable. It never gives a basic or free variable. If it is a pivot column, the system is inconsistent.

questions.q: An echelon form of the augmented matrix of a system in x1, x2, x3 is [1 4 -2 | 3; 0 0 5 | 1; 0 0 0 | 0]. What can you conclude?
choices: Cannot tell without the reduced echelon form
questions.explain: There is no row [0 0 0 | b] with b nonzero, so the system is consistent. The pivots are in columns 1 and 3, so column 2 (x2) has no pivot and x2 is free. A consistent system with a free variable has infinitely many solutions. An echelon form is enough to decide this.

questions.q: An echelon form of the augmented matrix of a system in x1, x2 is [1 2 | 1; 0 3 | 6; 0 0 | 0]. What can you conclude?
choices: Cannot tell without the reduced echelon form
questions.explain: The zero row says 0 = 0, which does no harm. The last column is not a pivot column, so the system is consistent. Both coefficient columns are pivot columns, so there are no free variables and the solution is unique (x2 = 2, x1 = -3).

questions.q: An echelon form of the augmented matrix of a system in x1, x2, x3 is [1 -1 2 | 4; 0 2 1 | 3; 0 0 0 | -7]. What can you conclude?
choices: Cannot tell without the reduced echelon form
questions.explain: The last row says 0x1 + 0x2 + 0x3 = -7, that is 0 = -7, which is impossible. The rightmost column is a pivot column, so the system has no solution.

questions.q: An echelon form of the augmented matrix of a system in x1, x2, x3 is [3 1 0 | 2; 0 -1 4 | 0; 0 0 2 | 5]. What can you conclude?
choices: Cannot tell without the reduced echelon form
questions.explain: Every coefficient column (1, 2, 3) is a pivot column and the last column is not, so the system is consistent with no free variables. The solution is unique. The pivots do not need to be 1 to decide this.

questions.q: True or false: if an echelon form of an augmented matrix has a row of all zeros [0 0 ... 0 | 0], the system has infinitely many solutions.
questions.explain: A zero row says 0 = 0 and does not by itself mean infinitely many solutions. For example, [1 0 | 1; 0 1 | 2; 0 0 | 0] has a zero row, but both variables are basic and the solution is unique. Infinitely many solutions requires a consistent system AND a free variable.

questions.q: True or false: if the coefficient matrix of a system has a pivot in every column, the system has exactly one solution.
questions.explain: A pivot in every coefficient column only rules out free variables. The system can still be inconsistent if the rightmost column of the augmented matrix is a pivot column. Example: x1 = 1 and x1 = 2 reduce to [1 | 1; 0 | 1], which has no solution.

questions.q: True or false: a consistent linear system with more variables than equations must have infinitely many solutions.
questions.explain: Each pivot is in a different row, so there are at most m pivots (m = number of equations). With n > m variable columns, at least one coefficient column has no pivot, which gives a free variable. A consistent system with a free variable has infinitely many solutions.

questions.q: A system of 3 equations in 3 variables has a 3 x 4 augmented matrix. An echelon form of it has pivots in columns 1, 2, and 4. What can you conclude?
choices: The system has exactly one solution
The system has infinitely many solutions, with x3 free
Nothing until the reduced echelon form is found
questions.explain: Column 4 is the rightmost (constants) column. By the Existence and Uniqueness Theorem, a system is consistent if and only if the rightmost column is NOT a pivot column. Here it is a pivot column, so an echelon form contains a row [0 0 0 | b] with b nonzero.

questions.q: A linear system has 2 equations in 3 variables. Which outcomes are possible?
questions.explain: There are at most 2 pivots but 3 variable columns, so if the system is consistent at least one variable is free and there are infinitely many solutions. The system can also be inconsistent, for example x1 + x2 + x3 = 1 and x1 + x2 + x3 = 2. Exactly one solution is impossible here, and exactly two is never possible for any linear system.

questions.q: Solve the system x1 + 8x2 = 10, 5x1 + 45x2 = 5.
questions.explain: R2 ← R2 - 5R1 gives 5x2 = -45, so x2 = -9. Then x1 = 10 - 8(-9) = 82. Check: 82 - 72 = 10 and 410 - 405 = 5. Each of the other choices satisfies the first equation but not the second.

questions.q: Find the point (x, y) that lies on both lines x + y = 2 and x - 3y = 0. Enter the x-coordinate as a decimal.
Solve by row reduction: -x - 2y - 4z = 1, 2x + 6y + 14z = 2, 3x + 6y + 15z = -12. What is x?
Solve by row reduction: 7x1 + 5x2 + 3x3 = 12, -6x1 + x2 - 3x3 = -23, 2x1 + x3 = 7.
Apply the Row Reduction Algorithm to 2x1 + x2 - x3 = 6, x1 - x2 + 2x3 = 2, 3x1 + x3 = 4. What is the solution set?
choices: Infinitely many solutions with x3 free
Infinitely many solutions with x2 free
questions.explain: R1 ↔ R2, then R2 ← R2 - 2R1 and R3 ← R3 - 3R1 give [0 3 -5 | 2] and [0 3 -5 | -2]. R3 ← R3 - R2 gives [0 0 0 | -4], which says 0 = -4. Quick check: adding the first two equations gives 3x1 + x3 = 8, which contradicts 3x1 + x3 = 4.

questions.q: Solve by row reduction: x - y + 3z = 7, -3x + 2y + z = -5, -2x + y + 4z = 2.
questions.explain: R2 ← R2 + 3R1 and R3 ← R3 + 2R1 both give [0 -1 10 | 16], so R3 ← R3 - R2 gives a zero row. Then R2 ← -R2 gives [0 1 -10 | -16], and R1 ← R1 + R2 gives [1 0 -7 | -9]. So x - 7z = -9 and y - 10z = -16, with z free. Choice 3 leaves the basic variable x in terms of the basic variable y, so it is not a finished general solution.

questions.q: The system x - y + 3z = 7, -3x + 2y + z = -5, -2x + y + 4z = 2 has general solution x = -9 + 7z, y = -16 + 10z, z free. Which of these are solutions of the system?
questions.explain: Each choice of z gives one solution: z = 0 gives (-9, -16, 0), z = 1 gives (-2, -6, 1), and z = 2 gives (5, 4, 2). (7, 0, 0) satisfies the first equation but gives -21 instead of -5 in the second. (-9, -16, 1) gives -9 + 16 + 3 = 10 instead of 7 in the first.

questions.q: Find the general solution of the system in x1, x2, x3, x4 whose augmented matrix is [-2 4 1 4 | 8; -3 6 -1 1 | 7; 1 -2 2 3 | 1; 2 -4 5 8 | 4]. Which variables are free?
questions.explain: R1 ↔ R3, then clear column 1: rows 2-4 become [0 0 5 10 | 10], [0 0 5 10 | 10], [0 0 1 2 | 2]. Use the [0 0 1 2 | 2] row as the next pivot row and clear the others, which leaves two zero rows. The pivot columns are 1 and 3, so x2 and x4 are free. RREF gives x1 = -3 + 2x2 + x4 and x3 = 2 - 2x4.

questions.q: Solve by row reduction: -5x1 + 10x2 - 11x3 + 3x4 = 9, x1 - 2x2 + 4x3 + 2x4 = -8, -x1 + 2x2 - 2x3 + x4 = 1. The system has infinitely many solutions, but one variable has the same value in every solution. What is x3?
questions.explain: R1 ↔ R2, then R2 ← R2 + 5R1 and R3 ← R3 + R1 give [0 0 9 13 | -31] and [0 0 2 3 | -7]. R2 ← R2 - 4R3 gives [0 0 1 1 | -3]. R3 ← R3 - 2R2 gives [0 0 0 1 | -1]. So x4 = -1 and x3 = -3 - x4 = -2. Column 2 has no pivot, so x2 is free and x1 = 2 + 2x2.

questions.q: Solve by row reduction: x1 + x2 + 2x3 = 9, 2x1 + 4x2 - 3x3 = 1, 3x1 + 6x2 - 5x3 = 0. What is x3?
questions.explain: R2 ← R2 - 2R1 gives [0 2 -7 | -17]. R3 ← R3 - 3R1 gives [0 3 -11 | -27]. To avoid fractions, R3 ← 2R3 gives [0 6 -22 | -54], then R3 ← R3 - 3R2 gives [0 0 -1 | -3], so x3 = 3. Back-substituting gives x2 = 2 and x1 = 1. Check: 1 + 2 + 6 = 9, 2 + 8 - 9 = 1, 3 + 12 - 15 = 0.

questions.q: For which values of h and k is the system x1 + 2x2 = k, -3x1 + hx2 = 5 inconsistent?
questions.explain: R2 ← R2 + 3R1 gives [0  h + 6 | 5 + 3k]. If h ≠ -6 there is a pivot in column 2 and the solution is unique. If h = -6 the row is [0 0 | 5 + 3k]. It says 0 = nonzero (inconsistent) when k ≠ -5/3, and it is a zero row giving infinitely many solutions when k = -5/3.

questions.q: In the system x1 + 2x2 = k, -3x1 - 6x2 = 5 (that is, h = -6), which value of k gives infinitely many solutions? Enter a decimal.
questions.explain: R2 ← R2 + 3R1 gives [0 0 | 5 + 3k]. For infinitely many solutions this must be a zero row, so 5 + 3k = 0 and k = -5/3 ≈ -1.6667. Geometrically, the two lines are parallel, and they are the same line exactly when 5 = -3k.

questions.q: For which values of a and b is the system x1 + x2 + x3 = 1, x1 + 2x2 + bx3 = 1, x1 + ax2 + 3x3 = 1 inconsistent?
choices: For no values of a and b (it is never inconsistent)
questions.explain: R2 ← R2 - R1 and R3 ← R3 - R1 make the right-hand sides of rows 2 and 3 equal to 0, and they stay 0 through further replacements. A row [0 0 0 | nonzero] can never appear. Directly: (1, 0, 0) satisfies all three equations for every a and b.

questions.q: For which values of a and b does the system x1 + x2 + x3 = 1, x1 + 2x2 + bx3 = 1, x1 + ax2 + 3x3 = 1 have infinitely many solutions?
questions.explain: R2 ← R2 - R1 and R3 ← R3 - R1 give [0 1 b-1 | 0] and [0 a-1 2 | 0]. R3 ← R3 - (a-1)R2 gives [0 0 2 - (a-1)(b-1) | 0]. When (a-1)(b-1) = 2 this is a zero row, x3 is free, and there are infinitely many solutions. a = 3, b = 2 is one such pair, but so is a = 2, b = 3, and many others.

questions.q: For which value of h is the system x1 + 3x2 = h, -2x1 - 6x2 = 4 consistent?
questions.explain: R2 ← R2 + 2R1 gives [0 0 | 4 + 2h]. The system is consistent only when 4 + 2h = 0, that is h = -2. Then x2 is free and there are infinitely many solutions. This system can never have exactly one solution.

questions.q: For which values of h and k does the system x1 - 2x2 = 3, 2x1 + hx2 = k have exactly one solution?
questions.explain: R2 ← R2 - 2R1 gives [0  h + 4 | k - 6]. If h + 4 ≠ 0, both coefficient columns are pivot columns and the solution is unique for every k. If h = -4, the system is inconsistent when k ≠ 6 and has infinitely many solutions when k = 6.

questions.q: For which values of h and k does the system x1 + x2 + x3 = 2, x2 + 2x3 = 1, x1 + 2x2 + hx3 = k have infinitely many solutions?
questions.explain: R3 ← R3 - R1 gives [0 1 h-1 | k-2]. R3 ← R3 - R2 gives [0 0 h-3 | k-3]. If h ≠ 3 the solution is unique. If h = 3 the row is [0 0 0 | k-3]: inconsistent when k ≠ 3, and a zero row (x3 free, infinitely many solutions) when k = 3.

questions.q: True or false: while row reducing a system that contains a parameter h, you can safely divide a row by h + 6 without considering separate cases.
questions.explain: h + 6 is zero when h = -6, and dividing by zero is not allowed (scaling must be by a nonzero scalar). Split into the cases h + 6 ≠ 0 (a pivot) and h + 6 = 0 (look at the right-hand side of that row).

questions.q: Evaluate Σ_{i=2}^{7} i² (the sum of i² for i from 2 to 7).
questions.explain: 2² + 3² + 4² + 5² + 6² + 7² = 4 + 9 + 16 + 25 + 36 + 49 = 139. Every term is i², and the sum starts at i = 2, not i = 1.

questions.q: Evaluate Σ_{i=1}^{4} (2i - 1).
questions.explain: Substitute i = 1, 2, 3, 4 and add: 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 = 16.

questions.q: What is the name of the Greek letter λ?
questions.explain: λ is lambda, σ is sigma (Σ is uppercase sigma), α is alpha, and β is beta.

questions.q: What set does N = {x ∈ R : x is a positive integer} describe?
questions.explain: Read it as 'the set of all x in R such that x is a positive integer'. x ∈ R means x is a real number, and the condition after the colon (sometimes written as a vertical bar) keeps only the positive integers.

questions.q: A 1080p (Full HD) video frame is 1920 x 1080 pixels. Each pixel stores 3 color components (red, green, blue), and each component is 1 byte. How many bytes does one uncompressed frame take?
questions.explain: 1920 · 1080 · 3 = 6,220,800 bytes. At 25 frames per second that is 155,520,000 bytes (about 155 MB) per second, which is why compression techniques such as the Singular Value Decomposition matter.

questions.q: Which of these applications needs only the solution of linear systems by row reduction, with no eigenvalues, determinants, or vector space theory?
choices: Network flow analysis (traffic or data flow)
Ranking web pages for a search engine
Image compression with the Singular Value Decomposition
Long-term employment prediction with a discrete-time dynamical system
questions.explain: Finding a general flow pattern in a network only requires setting up and row reducing a linear system. Web page ranking, the SVD, and dynamical systems also need eigenvalues and eigenvectors, along with other later topics.

questions.q: A state has 16.5 million employed and 1.2 million unemployed people. Each year 3% of the employed lose their jobs and 2% of the unemployed find one. How many people (in millions) are employed after one year?
questions.explain: Employed after one year = 16.5 - 0.03(16.5) + 0.02(1.2) = 16.5 - 0.495 + 0.024 = 16.029 million. The long-term behavior of this process is studied later with eigenvalues.
